rfi.title: ‘Welcome back’: Macron and Sanchez embrace prospect of UK return to EU
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has welcomed British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's reopening of the debate over the United Kingdom's relationship with the European Union, responding to the possibility of the UK eventually rejoining the bloc with a simple message in English: “Welcome back.”

rfi.title: Eiffel Tower chief to leave after women sidelined during Hindu visit
rfi.description: Eiffel Tower director Patrick Branco Ruivo will step down at the end of the year, the tower’s operator has announced, after female staff were excluded during a visit by a Hindu religious group – an incident that triggered a strike that closed the Paris landmark for a day.

rfi.title: Rugby World Cup bosses promise big party at first 24-team tournament
rfi.description: Organisers of the 2027 Rugby World Cup on Wednesday promised a massive party during the first 24-team tournament, which starts next October in Perth, Western Australia.

rfi.title: Exiled Burkina publisher tells RFI of repression and fear four years after coup
rfi.description: Burkina Faso on Wednesday marks four years since military strongman Captain Ibrahim Traoré took over in a coup. Comparing himself to anti-colonial icon Thomas Sankara, Traoré promised a "progressive and popular" revolution. RFI spoke to Inoussa Ouédraogo, a publishing director who now lives in exile about the country's fading human rights record.

rfi.title: Mali army and Russian fighters accused of killing dozens of civilians
rfi.description: Mali’s armed forces and Russian Wagner Group personnel committed war crimes including killings and torture of civilians during joint operations between 2023 and 2025, Amnesty International has said in a new report documenting abuses across several regions of the country.

rfi.title: US troops wrap up Iraq mission 12 years after Islamic State offensive
rfi.description: Iraq is closing a major chapter in its post-2003 history as the US-led coalition against Islamic State ends its mission – more than two decades after France opposed the invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein.

rfi.title: US Supreme Court lifts limits on third-country deportations
rfi.description: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday lifted restrictions on the deportations of immigrants to countries that are not their own, while agreeing to hear the issue on its merits in December.

rfi.title: Heatwaves and wildfires drive extreme ozone pollution worldwide
rfi.description: Heatwaves, wildfires and human-caused emissions exposed a third of the world’s population to extremely high ozone pollution in 2026, with Asia worst hit and wildfire smoke crossing oceans, an EU report said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Le Pen ally Bardella sues over antisemitism claims, alleges 'total war'
rfi.description: Jordan Bardella, a key ally of French far-right presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, on Tuesday said allegations he made antisemitic comments in 2013 marked part of a "total war" against their National Rally party ahead of the 2027 polls. Backed by fellow party members, Bardella announced that he had filed a complaint for defamation.

rfi.title: Ghana boss Queiroz refuses to quit after poor start to 2027 AFCON qualifiers
rfi.description: Ghana head coach Carlos Queiroz on Wednesday refused to resign after his side's calamitous 4-2 defeat at home to Gambia in qualifiers for next year's Africa Cup of Nations in Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda.

rfi.title: French PM warns against student violence as public sector strike kicks off
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has warned against an escalation of the demonstrations in secondary schools, which have broken out ahead of a nationwide strike by public-sector workers. More than 100 pupils were arrested on Monday during violent clashes with police. It comes amid mounting anger over the national budget, which is due to be unveiled on Thursday.

rfi.title: French public sector workers strike over pay freeze ahead of 2027 budget
rfi.description: Teachers, healthcare workers, local government staff, tax officials and firefighters in France are on strike Tuesday to pressure the government ahead of the 2027 budget debates which could see public sector salaries frozen for a fourth straight year.

rfi.title: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger launch Tafouk TV channel to push their own narrative
rfi.description: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are stepping up their joint media push with Tafouk TV, a new television channel aimed at challenging Western coverage and promoting the three military-led Sahel states’ own account of events.

rfi.title: French prosecutors seek 'severe' punishment for ex-minister Dati in graft case
rfi.description: France prosecutors on Monday sought two years with an electronic tag and a five-year ban on public office for ex-culture minister Rachida Dati in a trial on corruption charges linked to dealings with the Renault-Nissan group. Her lawyers have slammed the severity of the recommendations which will be announced in January next year.

rfi.title: US has 'alienated' Sudan's army in 'complex war' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has vowed to push on with his fight against the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, despite a US visa snub to attend the UN General Assembly and mounting pressure for a ceasefire. RFI spoke to a Sudanese researcher about why such a step was taken and how far the stand-off could go.

rfi.title: Egypt, Senegal and Ghana face pressure to relaunch drive for 2027 AFCON
rfi.description: Continental powerhouses Egypt, Ghana and Senegal will attempt to get their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaigns back on track on Tuesday after opening round setbacks last week.

rfi.title: Old hand Olise rewards Zidane's fresh blood adventure in Belgium
rfi.description: Michael Olise came off the substitutes bench on Monday night to score a sensational late goal for France against Belgium to give new boss Zinedine Zidane his second victory in two matches.

rfi.title: French church abuse victims praise Pope Leo for 'extraordinary' empathy
rfi.description: French victims of clerical abuse called their meeting with Pope Leo XIV on Sunday "extraordinary", praising him for listening deeply to their experiences. The Pope said he was committed to preventing further harm.

euronews.description: Sánchez and Macron back cooperation between Spain and France and call for greater EU unity on migration, economic and geopolitical issues, despite the Spanish Senate's rejection of the bilateral Friendship Treaty.

euronews.description: Uzeyir Hajibeyli’s musical legacy continues to bring different traditions together, inspiring an international festival spanning concerts, culture and musical exchange.

euronews.title: ‘There is no immediate threat to NATO territory,’ Secretary General Rutte tells Euronews
euronews.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte told Euronews there is no immediate threat to the alliance and he does not take Russia's Kaliningrad nuclear warning seriously, saying Moscow is trying to distract from its struggles in Ukraine.

euronews.title: BMW's strategy: Job cuts, AI and a €2bn bet on ‘Made in Germany’
euronews.description: German premium carmaker BMW Group is investing around €2 billion in vehicle production and battery manufacturing in Germany, as it unveils plans to rebuild profitability.

euronews.title: ‘Let workers have a say’: Protesters target OpenAI conference
euronews.description: Dozens of activists protested outside OpenAI's developer conference in San Francisco, calling on the company to end its contracts with the US military and Immigration and Customs Enforcement and demanding greater regulation of AI.

euronews.title: Spain to investigate claims its soldiers have tortured migrants in Ceuta
euronews.description: Amnesty International says it has documented beatings, humiliations, summary expulsions and racial profiling in Ceuta and the Spanish government has ordered the military to identify any individuals potentially responsible.

euronews.title: These 10 airlines have the best in-flight wifi – and only one is European
euronews.description: If you’re looking to get online while in the air, you might just want to book a flight with Qatar Airways, Delta or United.

euronews.title: EU-backed scheme helps rural Swedish households on lower incomes go electric
euronews.description: A Swedish government scheme, part-funded by the EU's Social Climate Fund, is offering rural, lower-income drivers financial support to switch from petrol and diesel to electric vehicles.

euronews.title: Grand Voyager | Exploring Berlin beyond the landmarks
euronews.description: Berlin is a city filled with history, creativity and energy, from street art on the Berlin Wall to cycling through its leafy streets. In this episode, Lilly Douse discovers what brings Germany’s capital to life.

euronews.title: Kubilius: Europe's response to Russian hybrid attacks should be 'as painful' for Moscow
euronews.description: The European Commissioner for Defence tells Euronews that the EU must sharpen its response to a growing spate of hybrid attacks attributed to Moscow, while rejecting those who say it's time to engage the Kremlin in diplomacy.

euronews.title: Bulgaria's parliament passes law protecting journalists from abusive SLAPP lawsuits
euronews.description: Most SLAPPs are for defamation or reputational harm and tend to be used by those rich and powerful enough to afford the necessary lawyers' fees.

euronews.title: US presses Europe to release more emergency oil reserves as prices surge
euronews.description: Washington says European countries have yet to deliver promised oil releases, as soaring crude and diesel prices intensify pressure on governments to intervene.

euronews.title: Inflation accelerates again in Italy: September rate hits 4.2%, a three-year high
euronews.description: Consumer price index accelerates driven by energy goods and fresh food. Between historical memory and daily worries, Istat records a sharp drop in confidence among households and firms.

euronews.title: No more radio silence: EU plans cross-border lifeline for emergency services
euronews.description: When disaster strikes near a border, police and firefighters can lose contact the moment they cross it. Brussels wants a 5G network, backed by satellites, to change that by 2036.

lemonde.title: Après la tentative de détournement d’un avion de Flydubai volant vers Tel-Aviv, des témoignages et des zones d’ombre
lemonde.description: Le vol Flydubai reliant Dubaï à Tel-Aviv a atterri en urgence en Arabie saoudite, après qu’un des pilotes a poignardé l’autre. Les autorités israéliennes n’excluent ni une attaque terroriste ni un geste suicidaire. Benyamin Nétanyahou avait mis en garde, la veille, contre des attaques éventuelles avant les élections législatives prévues pour le 27 octobre.

lemonde.title: Emmanuel Macron juge les propos antisémites imputés à Jordan Bardella « gravissimes et inacceptables » ; le président du RN lui répond
lemonde.description: Le chef de l’Etat a réagi, de Madrid, à l’enquête de « Mediapart » qui rapporte des propos antisémites de Jordan Bardella lorsqu’il était jeune militant du FN. « Après le 7 octobre 2023, j’ai marché dans les rues de Paris, et me suis rendu en Israël. Pas lui », a réagi le président du RN.

lemonde.title: « Ce n’était pas la DZ, c’était moi » : des rivalités entre narcotrafiquants derrière les menaces qui ont visé le maire d’Alès
lemonde.description: Un homme de 20 ans, gérant d’une boucherie dans la ville du Gard, a été mis en examen et écroué, mardi 29 septembre, dans l’enquête sur les menaces de mort visant l’élu. Selon les informations du « Monde », il a reconnu en garde à vue son implication et le fait d’avoir usurpé le nom de la DZ Mafia pour se venger.

lemonde.title: « Le danger des épisodes méditerranéens », comme celui qui touche le Sud-Est actuellement, « ce sont les crues éclair : tout déborde très vite »
lemonde.description: Alors que des pluies diluviennes tombent sur le sud-est de la France, le chercheur Philippe Drobinski rappelle, dans un entretien au « Monde », que le réchauffement climatique rend ces événements plus extrêmes.

lemonde.title: « L’accord sur le Groenland constitue le parfait contre-pied à la “diplomatie de la famille et des amis” de Donald Trump »
lemonde.description: A rebours des échecs au Moyen-Orient, où les discussions sont conduites par des non-diplomates proches du président américain, l’accord signé le 22 septembre entre le Danemark, le Groenland et les Etats-Unis s’est fait dans le respect des règles, au bénéfice de ses signataires, constate dans sa chronique Gilles Paris, éditorialiste au « Monde ».

lemonde.title: L’humoriste Paul Mirabel se dévoile avec autodérision dans sa série « Paul »
lemonde.description: Coécrite avec Mourad Boudaoud, Johan Gromb et Nathanael Munnich, cette série en six épisodes est nourrie d’anecdotes réelles vécues par le faux flegmatique.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : des coupures d’urgence d’électricité à Kiev et dans trois régions d’Ukraine après de nouvelles attaques russes
lemonde.description: Ces coupures dans certains secteurs de la capitale ukrainienne et des régions de Kiev, Tchernihiv et Jytomyr ont été décidées par l’opérateur Ukrenergo en raison d’une surcharge des équipements provoquée par les bombardements, selon l’entreprise publique.

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : Sébastien Lecornu alerte sur les risques d’une crise financière en France à la veille de présenter un projet de « redressement »
lemonde.description: Les taux d’intérêt à dix ans auxquels la France refinance sa dette sur les marchés ont dépassé, mardi, 4,8 %, pour la première fois depuis 2008.

lemonde.title: Baisser la TVA sur les carburants : la proposition de Marine Le Pen est-elle réaliste ?
lemonde.description: Illégale, chère, non ciblée, anti-écolo… Passage en revue des principales critiques à propos de la promesse phare du Rassemblement national pour faire baisser les prix à la pompe.

lemonde.title: Blocage des lycées : la mobilisation se poursuit, un syndicat veut rencontrer le ministre de l’éducation et annonce une « mobilisation commune » avec les étudiants
lemonde.description: Edouard Geffray a exprimé son inquiétude face à l’usage de la violence lors des blocages, tout en soulignant que certaines revendications étaient « légitimes ». De Madrid, Emmanuel Macron a dit qu’« aucune de ces craintes ne légitime la violence ».

lemonde.title: Réductions et crédits d’impôt : des avantages conséquents pour un nombre limité de foyers aux revenus élevés
lemonde.description: Dans un rapport publié mercredi 30 septembre, le Conseil des prélèvements obligatoires porte un regard critique sur la répartition des dispositifs selon les niveaux de ressources. Il préconise de renforcer leur plafonnement et de reconsidérer les modalités de calcul de la contribution différentielle sur les hauts revenus.

lemonde.title: « Le dilemme » : faut-il taper ses symptômes dans Google ou ChatGPT, au risque d’alimenter nos peurs ?
lemonde.description: Chaque mois, nos dilemmes moraux intimes sont passés au crible. Une tache sur la peau, une douleur au genou : l’angoisse nous saisit. Trouver la cause de cette manifestation est désormais si simple grâce au Net, même si le diagnostic peut être erroné.

lemonde.title: La justice américaine suspend l’exécution de Christa Pike, quelques minutes avant l’injection létale prévue
lemonde.description: Reconnue coupable d’avoir torturé et assassiné Colleen Slemmer, sa camarade d’école, en 1995, quand elle avait 18 ans, elle devait être la première femme mise à mort aux Etats-Unis depuis 2023.

lemonde.title: Après la reconnaissance de la rafle du Vieux-Port de Marseille comme crime contre l’humanité, le soulagement des victimes : « C’est la fin de l’indifférence collective »
lemonde.description: Au terme d’une enquête de sept ans, poussée par la mobilisation des victimes, le parquet national antiterroriste donne une qualification à l’opération conjointe des forces nazies et de Vichy qui a touché 20 000 Marseillais en janvier 1943.

lemonde.title: Le « climat incestuel », cette violence sans passage à l’acte qui doit alerter
lemonde.description: A la veille de l’examen de la loi intégrale contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles devant l’Assemblée nationale, la notion d’« incestuel » explorée par plusieurs auteurs et chercheurs, propose de ne plus circonscrire l’inceste aux agressions elles-mêmes, mais de le penser comme s’inscrivant souvent dans un climat ambiant.

lemonde.title: Noisy-le-Sec : le tribunal administratif annule les élections municipales à cause de déclarations de candidatures non conformes
lemonde.description: Les parties ont jusqu’au 30 octobre pour faire appel devant le Conseil d’Etat. En cas d’annulation définitive, une nouvelle élection devra être organisée dans les trois mois.

phys-org.description: When you order food through an app, how much do you know about where you're buying it from? It could be a restaurant on the local main street or one located in a warehouse in a faraway industrial park.

phys-org.title: Earth and Mars: Built from different cosmic recipes
phys-org.description: Four and a half billion years ago, Earth and Mars were born in the rotating cloud of gas and dust that would eventually become our solar system. Yet exactly how the planets formed remains one of the most disputed questions in planetary science.

phys-org.title: Cities across the world are sinking because of groundwater depletion, but the process can be reversed
phys-org.description: Many cities around the world are sinking because too much water is extracted from the groundwater reservoirs beneath them. This sinking makes these coastal cities more exposed to rising seas as the climate warms. But as our new research shows, this process can work in reverse: When groundwater is replenished, cities can rise.

phys-org.title: Alpine bacteria show unexpected ability to fight viruses
phys-org.description: A silent, long-running competition has been taking place in Swiss alpine lakes for millions of years, killing trillions of organisms every day without anyone noticing. This competition between bacteria and viruses pushes both into a relentless evolutionary battle.

phys-org.title: Drones, satellites and AI help scientists watch over Antarctica's smallest lifeforms
phys-org.description: Monitoring Antarctica's tiny, scattered ecosystems is a challenge that has long plagued researchers. But a new study led by the University of Wollongong (UOW) offers a new approach to tracking life in one of the most remote environments on Earth. The research is published in the ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing.

phys-org.title: Q&A: The safety and sterilization of pharmaceuticals manufacturing
phys-org.description: Manufacturing modern medicines is a multistage process, and each step introduces the opportunity for contamination, which can be both deadly and expensive. Recently, epinephrine injections, used for severe allergic reactions, were recalled due to a lack of assurance of sterility, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

phys-org.title: Light-activated crystals break down DNA-like molecules in water, potentially curbing antibiotic resistance
phys-org.description: Engineers have developed a new approach for turning ordinary water into a weapon against antibiotic-resistant bacteria, according to a study published in the journal Chem Catalysis.

phys-org.title: Butterflies use optical illusions to dodge predators
phys-org.description: A bird attacking a butterfly will often find its beak snapping at thin air. According to new research, that split-second miss isn't just bad luck. It's caused by a visual illusion from the butterfly's wings.

phys-org.title: Asgard archaea suggest crawling motility may be far older than previously thought
phys-org.description: Asgard archaea, our closest known microbial relatives, play a key role in current models of the origin of more complex organisms, known as eukaryotes (all animals, plants, protists and fungi). However, their biology has so far been poorly understood.

phys-org.title: Little-studied Antarctic basin could raise sea levels, but melt timing remains unknown
phys-org.description: Over a century ago, Australian geologist Sir Douglas Mawson led a sledding expedition over hundreds of kilometers of ice into a remote part of East Antarctica. The party turned back after the tragic death of a party member. Fellow Australian Cecil Madigan led another group across sea ice into the region before also turning back.

phys-org.title: Physicists identify 'octupolar' magnetism, with implications for quantum technologies
phys-org.description: Most magnets have two poles: north and south, or positive and negative, in a familiar arrangement called a "dipole." But researchers are increasingly uncovering more complex forms of magnetism.

phys-org.title: Study: Paid internships deliver strong payoff early in careers
phys-org.description: A new national study co-authored by UW–Madison School of Education professor Mindi Thompson, who directs the university's Center for Research on College‑Workforce Transitions (CCWT), offers evidence that paid internships give college graduates a lasting advantage in earnings, job quality and early career progression.

phys-org.title: Lost shark becomes viral star in South Korea
phys-org.description: A wayward shark has become an unlikely celebrity in South Korea, drawing massive crowds, earning plaudits from the local mayor and even moving the stock market.

phys-org.title: As El Niño strengthens across the Pacific, Australian farmers could face fierce frosts
phys-org.description: In the highlands of Papua New Guinea, crops have been killed by drought and frost. Severe frosts have destroyed food crops such as taro, sweet potatoes, bananas and sugarcane, leaving some local communities scrambling for food.

phys-org.title: Pigeon fathers take on more responsibility when times get tough
phys-org.description: A study published in the journal Royal Society Open Science by researchers at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) shows that when food becomes scarce, male pigeons spend more time incubating eggs, allowing females additional time to forage for themselves.

phys-org.title: Climate refuges may be key to restoring imperiled amphibians
phys-org.description: As a deadly fungal disease ravages wild frog populations around the globe, scientists have identified potential locations in Panama where amphibians might persist despite the disease, according to new research from the Smithsonian's National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute (NZCBI) and Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI) published in the Journal for Nature Conservation.

phys-org.title: Research shows how AI is getting better at exams: How universities can respond
phys-org.description: When ChatGPT arrived at the end of 2022, universities scrambled to determine whether generative AI was good enough to pass assessments and make it easy for students to cheat.

phys-org.title: Study reveals how tilapia adapt to extreme salt stress
phys-org.description: In the world of aquatic life, the Mozambique tilapia (Oreochromis mossambicus) is remarkably tolerant of saltwater, surviving in habitats ranging from fresh water to hypersaline ponds three times saltier than the ocean.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

undark.title: Book Excerpt: Why the Brain Isn’t the Self
undark.description: The brain isn’t the self — consciousness is intimately linked with the human body. And if consciousness is the body’s way of knowing itself, then it is the living form in its entirety that should be taken as selfhood proper, with the brain as an especially feverish region.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
proj-syn.description: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.

proj-syn.title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
proj-syn.description: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

proj-syn.title: Is Another Eurozone Debt Crisis Looming?
proj-syn.description: At a time when the cost of servicing sovereign debt is rising globally, France stands out as an especially fragile case. Its public debt-to-GDP ratio is edging up toward that of Greece on the eve of its sovereign-debt crisis, and the French political system seems unable to do anything about it.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Reverse the Renminbi’s Rise?
proj-syn.description: In China, AI-driven productivity gains will most likely be in non-tradable services, which could push down relative prices and put downward pressure on the renminbi’s real exchange rate. To ensure that this does not also mean lower income and weaker demand, policymakers should ensure that the productivity dividend is broadly shared.

proj-syn.title: The Price of You
proj-syn.description: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data. AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.

proj-syn.title: Investing in Brain Health
proj-syn.description: Just as AI agents are mastering complex cognitive tasks, our own ability to perform the same tasks is eroding. Whether AI vindicates its boosters or fizzles out like the Metaverse craze of 2022, we will not fare well without a civilization-wide effort to rebuild the cognitive skills that make technological progress possible.

proj-syn.title: Europe Still Needs Molecules
proj-syn.description: Not even the most effective European electrification strategy will eliminate the need for the molecules that fossil fuels provide. Given this, Europe must diversify its oil and gas supplies, maintain its refining capacity, and lock in decarbonization by building a hydrogen-energy industry at scale.

proj-syn.title: Energy Security in an Age of Disruption
proj-syn.description: While there is no single prescription for energy security, strengthening “response capacity,” such as by establishing stockpiles, substituting sources, and diversifying suppliers, is essential. The point is not to eliminate vulnerabilities altogether, but to ensure that there are options when disruption arrives.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Common Currency-in-Waiting
proj-syn.description: While the phased approach of the Economic Community of West African States to implementing a long-delayed single currency will maintain momentum without compromising macroeconomic discipline, the bloc still lacks a robust mechanism to address asymmetric shocks. That is why fiscal integration must come first.

proj-syn.title: Learning to Reconcile
proj-syn.description: Political discourse in many Western countries has broken down, making it difficult for people with different viewpoints to live amicably with one another. The Reconciliation League, an international initiative by 13 universities and colleges, aims to train a generation of leaders who can change that.

proj-syn.title: Sheinbaum Is Just Another Trump Appeaser
proj-syn.description: After two years in office, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum continues to be widely praised, both in Mexico and abroad, for her handling of US President Donald Trump. But Sheinbaum has skillfully—and cynically—disguised the extent to which she has deferred to Trump on almost every issue.

proj-syn.title: Distorted Intelligence at the AI Frontier
proj-syn.description: The real problem for the frontier AI labs is not that their models are too powerful and already “misaligned” with the goals their creators set for them. Rather, it is that the models are being trained in ways that may be leading to a type of intelligence that will become less predictable.

proj-syn.title: Good Growth Requires the Right Public Finance
proj-syn.description: Although the Labour Party has done more to strengthen the United Kingdom's public-finance ecosystem in the past two years than any government in a generation, it must not stop there. If public investment is to meet its full potential, it must be reorganized to operate at scale on the public's behalf.

proj-syn.title: An EU–Canada Partnership Against Coercion

proj-syn.title: The Opposing Forces Reshaping Global Finance
proj-syn.description: The financial industry is being pulled between two powerful forces: bottom-up financial technology is enabling seamless integration, while top-down geoeconomic statecraft is promoting fragmentation. So much for the conventional wisdom that finance will simply become smoother, cheaper, and more globalized over time.

proj-syn.title: The Dismally Obedient Science
proj-syn.description: While empirical inquiry has its place in economics, the pursuit of causality must not be allowed to displace the pursuit of explanation. Beyond identifying causal effects within existing arrangements, economists must investigate how those arrangements are produced, reproduced, and contested.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchy Is a Symptom, Not a Cause
proj-syn.description: The deepening political dysfunction plaguing the US can be traced not to wealth inequality, as some argue, but to the fact that different groups of voters believe different facts. A political strategy that takes this into account might eventually lead to wealth redistribution, but it must begin with improved critical-thinking skills.

proj-syn.title: The Immigrants Leading the Anti-Immigrant Far Right
proj-syn.description: Right-wing populists have turned hypocrisy into a successful electoral strategy. But those voting for nativism in Europe and the United States should be careful what they wish for: They may end up expelling their own family members, if not their own political leaders.
